notes: The whole app moves on one set of curves now. Every surface used to spell out its own timing, so two things that arrived together did not settle together; there is one set of durations and three curves, and arrivals, drops, sheets and fades all read them.

A tap answers. Tabs, playlist rows, settings rows and pick buttons compress a little under your finger and come back on release — it is a transform, so the compositor does it and nothing on the page has to be re-laid-out.

Switching tabs cross-fades instead of cutting. The page uses the phone’s own view transition: the frame you are leaving fades out over the one you asked for, in a single pass, with the change itself running exactly when it ran before. An older WebView simply switches the way it always did.
A scroll belongs to the pane it started in. Reaching the end of the tab strip, a settings pane or the Studio list no longer drags the page behind it, and momentum scrolling stays on.

Settings panes settle in when you switch to them, with the same arrival the main views get — and Reduce motion in Sandbox, or the phone’s own setting, turns all of it off. The state still changes; nothing travels.

New theme: Prism — cool and glassy at the top of the screen, warm under it, with the accent light enough to read on both. Four layers of colour drift behind the whole app. Free, like every theme has been since the badge wall came down.
